subject: Request: Staggered remittance & Net-90 for pilot — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <s.ortiz@orchidhealth.io>
To: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchidhealth.io
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot PO and invoicing cadence question

Hi Ava / Jonas —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the pilot scope in the SOW looks good. Our finance team has one ask on the billing cadence: Orchid’s board-approved spend cadence for pilots is quarterly invoicing (one invoice per quarter), and our internal treasury policy is Net-90 on those quarterly invoices.

Practical ask: can Redwood accept quarterly invoicing with Net-90 terms for the first 12 months of the pilot? The PO is attached so you have the numbers (PO_Orchid_1001.pdf). We can sign the SOW immediately if terms can be accommodated; otherwise we’ll need to align on an alternative.

Appreciate your help — Samantha

Attachments: PO_Orchid_1001.pdf

Samantha Ortiz
Head of Procurement, Orchid Health
procurement@orchidhealth.io | +1 415-555-0198

From: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <s.ortiz@orchidhealth.io>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot PO and invoicing cadence question

Jonas / Marissa / Ben — looping you in for deal desk / finance guidance. Orchid Health (high-confidence logo) is asking for quarterly invoicing with Net-90 on those quarter invoices for year 1 of the pilot (approx $240k ARR run rate). PO attached by the buyer.

My read: Net-90 materially increases DSO and credit exposure. We can offer alternatives:
- Option A: Quarterly invoicing, Net-30 per invoice (standard) — customer keeps their cadence but payment expectations unchanged.
- Option B: Quarterly invoicing + Net-90, but trade for a commercial concession (revenue credit or 2–3% platform credit for year 1).
- Option C: Net-90 only if we get ACH pre-authorization or an escrow arrangement to mitigate risk.

Please advise constraint thresholds and anything we need for the approval packet (impact analysis, recommended concession, who needs to sign). If we proceed with Option B/C we’ll need exec sign-off + legal addendum in the SOW.

Jonas, can you ask the buyer which alternative they prefer (credit vs pre-authorization)? I’ll prepare the numbers for finance.

Thanks — Ava

Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0133

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot PO and invoicing cadence question

Team —

Thanks for flagging. Quick financial assessment:
- Exposure: If we accept Net-90 on quarterly invoices for a $240k ARR pilot, peak outstanding receivable could be ~ $180k at any point in the first year depending on ramp — not trivial for a pilot.
- Risk tolerance: Finance will approve exceptions up to Net-60 on standard terms for customers with established credit and references. Net-90 requires senior finance exec (Markus) sign-off and a mitigation plan.

Mitigation options (ranked):
1) ACH pre-authorization + auto-debit on invoice due date (preferred).
2) Escrow or letter of credit covering first two quarters.
3) Revenue credit (2%–3%) for accepting Net-90, applied as a year-end credit or invoice-level credit.

If sales needs Net-90, recommend we request a 2% platform credit + signed addendum that explicitly states interest at 1.5%/month after 30 days past due and revocation clause if >30 days delinquent on any invoice. Finance will prepare expected working capital impact for Markus.

Ben Carter
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Approval request — Orchid Health payment terms (Net-90 / quarterly)

Markus —

Forwarding for executive approval. Summary: Orchid Health (deal RDW-2027-1001) wants quarterly invoicing with Net-90 for the first 12 months. The AE believes they need the cadence to match Orchid’s board approvals; finance flagged material DSO impact and recommends either ACH pre-auth or a 2% revenue credit as trade. Legal will add an addendum with late-payment interest and revocation clause.

Requested from you: approval to proceed with Net-90 for year 1 on the following conditions:
- 2% platform credit applied to invoices for year 1 (or a similar revenue concession)
- ACH pre-authorization OR escrow covering first two quarters (preferred)
- Signed SOW + addendum via DocuSign
- Clause: interest at 1.5%/month after 30 days past due; rights to suspend service and revoke special terms on >30 days delinquency

I’ve attached the proposed SOW (Proposed_SOW_Orchid_v3.pdf) and the buyer PO. Finance has prepared impact numbers and is standing by to provide them if you need details.

If approved I’ll coordinate with Legal for the addendum and Jonas will confirm the buyer’s preferred mitigation.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Proposed_SOW_Orchid_v3.pdf, PO_Orchid_1001.pdf, ExecApprovalForm.docx

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: legal_team@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Approval request — Orchid Health payment terms (Net-90 / quarterly)

Thx for the clear packet. I approve a one-year Net-90 exception for Orchid Health under the following non-negotiable conditions:

1) Commercial concession: 2% platform credit applied to invoices for the first 12 months (documented in SOW addendum).
2) Mitigation: ACH pre-authorization is required; if buyer declines ACH we accept escrow covering Q1+Q2 as an alternative.
3) Contractual protections: addendum to SOW (via DocuSign) that includes: 1.5%/month interest after 30 days past due, explicit service suspension rights, and immediate revocation of the Net-90 concession upon any >30-day delinquency.
4) Timebox: This exception expires after 12 months from SOW execution; any extension requires re-approval by me and finance.
5) Finance deliverable: Ben to record expected working capital impact and confirm cash-flow monitoring cadence (monthly for first three months).

Jonas/Ava — proceed to confirm Orchids’ acceptance of the above. Legal: please prepare the addendum and the DocuSign package; include an ExecApprovalForm and mark this as an "exception" in our contract tracker.

Markus Klein
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0110
